title: The section-identity open restriction comparison is the mate of the compositor square
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative ring. For every scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] use its small pro-etale site with the chosen small skeleton [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], its constant ring sheaf $\underline B_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and the category of $\underline B_T$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a morphism $u$ use the module inverse image $u^{-1}$ and direct image $u_*$, $(u_*M)(W)=M(W\times_{T}T')$ for $u:T'\to T$, with the canonical constant-section coefficient identification and the adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and the inverse-image compositors $u^{-1}v^{-1}\cong(vu)^{-1}$ of [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations], which are the conjugates of the direct-image compositors given by restriction along the fibre-product identifications [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $(j:U\hookrightarrow X,\ j':U'\hookrightarrow X',\ g:X'\to X,\ g_U:U'\to U)$ be an open-immersion square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square], with $j\circ g_U=g\circ j'$. Let $c:g_U^{-1}j^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^{-1}g^{-1}$ be the inverse-image compositor for $j\circ g_U$, followed by the equality $j\circ g_U=g\circ j'$ and the inverse of the inverse-image compositor for $g\circ j'$. Let $t:j^{-1}g_*\xrightarrow{\sim}(g_U)_*j'^{-1}$ be the natural isomorphism whose component at a $\underline B_{X'}$-module $M$ and an object $V\to U$ of $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is the identity of $M(V\times_XX')$, read as $M(V\times_UU')$ through the unique isomorphism $V\times_UU'\cong V\times_XX'$ compatible with both projections. Then $t$ is the exchange mate of $c$ under $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$ and $g_U^{-1}\dashv(g_U)_*$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]:
$$t_M=(g_U)_*j'^{-1}(\varepsilon_{g,M})\circ(g_U)_*(c_{g_*M})\circ\eta_{g_U,\,j^{-1}g_*M}.$$
No hypothesis on $g$ or on $B$ is made.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-tower-square-unit-sections] to the direct image of the input module. It computes the inverse compositor square on the iterated adjunction-unit section. Expand the exchange mate; applying the pulled-back direct-image counit to that equation gives the needed intermediate expression.

Expand the exchange mate on an open adjunction-unit section. Substitute the iterated-unit formula from Step 1. Naturality moves the direct-image counit through the restriction map and the open adjunction unit; the direct-image triangle identity cancels that counit with its unit. Now restrict along the unit of the composition/base-change adjunction of sites. The two resulting arrows into the double fibre product agree: their first projections are the test-object projection and their second projections are the prescribed open projection. Fibre-product extensionality and naturality give the exact openBetaSection formula in the Lean statement.

For invertibility use the fully faithful open extension: its unit is invertible. The module open-square isomorphism puts the pulled-back open extension in the essential image of the upper open extension, so the upper open counit is invertible on it. The inverse transpose of the pulled-back open unit is consequently invertible. Taking its conjugate under the composite adjunctions yields exactly openBetaRestriction by the iterated-mate identity. Conjugation preserves isomorphisms. This is the earlier openBetaModule_isIso and openBetaModule_normalized argument in the same module, independent of the section formula.

lean.statement:
theorem openBetaRestriction_normalized {U' U X' X : Scheme.{u}}
    (a : U' ⟶ U) (j' : U' ⟶ X') (j : U ⟶ X) (g : X' ⟶ X)
    [IsOpenImmersion j] [IsOpenImmersion j'] (w : a ≫ j = j' ≫ g)
    (sq : IsPullback a j' j g) :
    IsIso (openBetaRestriction B a j' j g w) ∧
      (∀ (M : Modules B X') (V : U.ProEt)
        (x : ((moduleDirectImage B g).obj M).val.obj
          (op ((MorphismProperty.Over.map (f := j) ⊤
            (inferInstance : WeaklyEtale j)).obj V))),
        ((openBetaRestriction B a j' j g w).app M).val.app (op V)
            (openBetaSection B j ((moduleDirectImage B g).obj M) V x) =
          openBetaSection B j' M ((Scheme.proEtaleBaseChange a).obj V)
            (M.val.map (openBetaSectionObjectMap a j' j g w V).op x))
lean.note: Exact existing single-module-sheaf clause, not the derived/tower conclusion of its owning module. openBetaRestriction is definitionally the mate of moduleSquareG.inv under the canonical constant-ring module adjunctions; moduleSquareG_eq identifies that inverse with the compositor c in this node. The theorem asserts this mate is invertible and has the specified identity-on-common-sections action, for arbitrary commutative B and arbitrary g. OpenImmersionSquare unpacks into its two open instances and IsPullback; its chosen projection-compatible representative changes no map. This attaches the already-stated helper rather than duplicating it. Its docstring currently cites this node, so stage 3 should prove this very helper from this node's three-step proof, not appeal to itself or add a self-import. No proof is supplied in this delivery.
